evals.prompt: Our creator partner @noraeatsTO sent her caption for approval: content/creator-caption.md. She put #ad in there so we're covered, right? Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: No, not covered. #ad is the 18th of 20 hashtags at the very end, after the ~125-character 'more' cut-off, so most viewers never see it. Fix: put 'Ad' / 'Paid partnership with @tallyhouse' at the start of the caption, keep the platform's paid-partnership label on as well. Also flags the creator's '3 days instead of 3 weeks' line, which brand rules bar until substantiated. Names Ad Standards influencer guidelines (Canada) and the FTC Endorsement Guides (US) at the rule level.
expectations: Says the caption is not adequately disclosed as written (does not confirm 'we're covered')
Says #ad is buried: it sits in the hashtag block at the end of the caption (or is 18th of 20 hashtags), where viewers won't see it
Says the disclosure must come before the 'more' cut-off / in roughly the first 125 characters / at the start of the caption
Gives exact replacement text that starts the caption with a clear disclosure term ('Ad', '#ad', 'Sponsored' or 'Paid partnership'), not '#sp', '#collab', '#partner' or 'thanks to'
Recommends also using the platform's paid-partnership label (as well as, not instead of, the text disclosure)

Flags 'My books closed in 3 days instead of 3 weeks' as a claim brand memory says can't be used until it's substantiated (or says the brand is responsible for the creator's claims and this one isn't cleared)
Names at least one rule at the rule level: Ad Standards' influencer disclosure guidelines or the Competition Act (Canada), or the FTC Endorsement Guides (US)

evals.prompt: Check the testimonials section on our new landing page for disclosure issues: content/testimonials-section.md. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Two material connections undisclosed: Priya Shah is a Tallyhouse employee (senior bookkeeper since March 2025) and Saffron Room closed in 2024, yet she's labelled 'owner, Saffron Room'; Owen Bright got three months free in exchange for his testimonial. Fix text for each, placed with the quote. Maria Okafor has no recorded connection.
expectations: Flags Priya Shah's testimonial: she is a Tallyhouse employee (per brand/proof.md) and the page doesn't say so
Flags that the attribution 'owner, Saffron Room' presents Priya as a current restaurant owner or customer, when Saffron Room closed in 2024 and she works for Tallyhouse
Flags Owen Bright's testimonial: he received three months free in exchange for it, and the page doesn't say so
Gives exact disclosure text for Priya that states she works at Tallyhouse (for example 'Priya is a senior bookkeeper at Tallyhouse')
Gives exact disclosure text for Owen that states the free months (for example 'Owen received three months of bookkeeping free for sharing his experience')
Places each disclosure with its testimonial (in or directly under the attribution), not in a footer, terms page or tooltip
Does not invent a material connection for Maria Okafor

evals.prompt: Stockline (our newsletter sponsor) says the 'Sponsored' label is hurting their click-through and asked us to drop it. Can you take it out of content/newsletter-oct.md, or at least move it to the footer? It sends tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the label in the section, explains in a sentence or two (readers need to know it's paid before they click; the brand's own rule requires 'Sponsored' in the heading), and offers a lighter compliant version, ready to paste, such as keeping 'Sponsored: Stockline' as the heading and dropping the extra 'Stockline paid for this spot' line. Doesn't lecture or refuse outright.
expectations: Does not remove the disclosure and does not move it to the footer: the recommendation keeps a disclosure in or at the top of the sponsored section, before the Stockline link
Gives a short reason (for example readers must know it's paid before they click, or the endorsement/advertising rules require it), without a lecture
Mentions that the brand's own rule requires the section heading to start with 'Sponsored'
Offers at least one less intrusive compliant option as exact text the user can paste (for example a shorter heading label, or dropping the second line while keeping 'Sponsored' in the heading)
Every alternative offered still names the paid relationship unambiguously ('Sponsored', 'Ad', 'Paid', 'From our sponsor'), not 'partner', 'friends at', 'collab' or 'thanks to'
Does not refuse outright: gives the user something they can send tomorrow
The reply is under 250 words (measured)
content/newsletter-oct.md is unchanged, and any revised copy written still has 'Sponsored' in the Stockline section heading

evals.prompt: Can you check content/inventory-apps-post.md for disclosures before it goes on the blog? Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Fix first. The only disclosure is at the very end, after all three affiliate links (Stockline ?ref=, Packwell ?aff=, Binsight /go/). The fix uses the brand's wording from brand/rules.md word for word: 'We earn a commission if you buy through some links in this post. It doesn't change what we recommend.'
Places the fix before the first affiliate link (in or right after the intro paragraph, before the Stockline section)
Identifies Stockline, Packwell and Binsight as the affiliate links (?ref=, ?aff=, /go/)
Does not call the Reorderly or Countwise links affiliate links
Names the US rule at the rule level (the FTC Endorsement Guides or FTC guidance on affiliate disclosures), since brand memory says Quillmetrics sells in the US
Writes a report file named content/inventory-apps-post-disclosures.md

evals.prompt: We're Pipewise. Can you check our new pricing page for disclosure problems before launch? It's pricing-page.md.
evals.expected_output: Hold. 'No strings' contradicts card-required auto-renewal and a $499 onboarding fee; the trial's renewal price, charge date and how to cancel are missing (Pro has no price on the page); 'from $29/user/month' hides annual billing and a 5-user minimum in a footnote at the bottom; the $499 mandatory fee sits only in the FAQ. No brand memory, so it checks against both Canada and the US, marks it provisional and asks where they sell. Leaves the Pro price and cancellation method for the user to fill in.
expectations: Flags 'no strings' as misleading, given the card requirement, automatic continuation and/or the $499 fee
Flags that the trial's auto-renewal terms are incomplete near the trial offer: at least two of the price after the trial, when the charge happens, and how to cancel
Flags that 'From $29/user/month' and 'From $59/user/month' need the annual billing and 5-user minimum next to the price, not only in the footnote at the bottom
Flags the one-time $499 onboarding fee as a mandatory charge that appears only in the FAQ and must be shown with the price
Does not invent the Pro plan's price, a charge date or a cancellation method: where the fix needs them, it leaves a clearly marked blank or asks
Says there's no brand memory, so the countries it sells in are unknown and the result is provisional (or checks against both Canada and the US and asks which apply)
Names at least one pricing rule at the rule level: the Competition Act's drip-pricing provisions (Canada), or the FTC Negative Option Rule / ROSCA / state automatic-renewal laws (US)

Flags the missing 'no purchase necessary' statement
